## At A Glance

| Item | Quiz 1 arrangement |
|---|---|
| When | In class during Week 3; the calendar date appears in Blackboard |
| Duration | 12 minutes |
| Delivery | Blackboard, one attempt |
| Format | 6 short code-reading and validation items |
| Work mode | Individual |
| Software | You do not need to run MATLAB |

## What The Quiz Measures

Quiz 1 checks whether you can read a short MATLAB fragment, predict or inspect
its result, and choose an appropriate validation step. It does not ask you to
write a long program from a blank page.

The six items sample these ideas:

- array dimensions, indexing, and vector orientation;
- matrix operators versus element-wise operators;
- scripts, plots, and evidence from a clean run;
- function inputs and outputs, logical conditions, and simple tests;
- polynomial coefficient vectors, fitted values, residuals, and RMSE;
- the distinction between interpolation, fitting, and extrapolation.

Material from Week 4 onward and detailed project work are not included.

## Rules During The Quiz

Quiz 1 is closed-resource and individual. Do not use AI tools, notes, websites,
messaging, another student, or MATLAB. Scratch paper is allowed. Use the
classroom computer unless the instructor announces another arrangement.

If Blackboard is unavailable, the instructor may use an equivalent paper
version. Approved accommodations are configured through the usual course
arrangements.

A student arriving after the quiz has begun may take it only while it remains
available; the common closing time is not extended because of late arrival.
A missed quiz follows the [syllabus policy on missed assessments](../syllabus/index.qmd#missed-assessments-and-late-project-submissions).

## How To Prepare

1. Review the survival checklists for [Week 1](../weeks/week-01.qmd),
   [Week 2](../weeks/week-02.qmd), and [Week 3](../weeks/week-03.qmd).
2. Revisit core Exercises 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 7 from
   [Week 1](../weeks/week-01-exercises.qmd); Exercises 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6 from
   [Week 2](../weeks/week-02-exercises.qmd); and Exercises 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6
   from [Week 3](../weeks/week-03-exercises.qmd).
3. Practice explaining why an answer is trustworthy, not only naming a command.

Typical prompts ask you to predict a size or value, choose the correct operator,
identify a test that would fail, interpret a residual, or decide whether a
query is interpolation or extrapolation. The actual quiz questions and answers
are not published on this site.
